title: Review: The ionic model; The covalent model
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: S2.2#c09 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.2#c14 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; S2.1.3#xt1 term and clue written for the game; S2.1.3#xt2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: S2.1#q12, S2.2#q02, S2.2#q38, S2.2#q04, S2.1#q13, S2.2#q37, S2.2#q03, S2.2#q39, S2.1#q14, S2.2#q01, S2.1#q15, S2.1#q10. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Coordination bond
items.clue: A shared pair in which both electrons come from the same atom.

items.label: Electronegativity
items.clue: The ability of an atom to attract a shared pair in a covalent bond.

items.label: Ionic lattice
items.clue: Regular three-dimensional arrangement of oppositely charged particles, such as Na⁺ and Cl⁻.

items.label: Lattice enthalpy
items.clue: Energy measure of the strength of bonding in a salt; larger for small, highly charged ions.

questions.stem: Sodium chloride dissolves in water but not in hexane, C₆H₁₄. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Water lowers the melting point of NaCl so that it melts at room temperature.
The ions fit into the spaces between water molecules but not hexane ones.
Polar water molecules are attracted to the ions and separate them from the lattice.
Water turns the neutral NaCl units into ions, which then spread out.

questions.explanation: Water molecules are polar: their partially negative O atoms are attracted to Na⁺ and their partially positive H atoms to Cl⁻, so the ions leave the lattice and are surrounded by water. Hexane is non-polar and is not attracted strongly enough to the ions.

questions.stem: Boron trichloride, BCl₃, is a covalent molecule (boron is in group 13; chlorine is in group 17). In its Lewis formula, how many electrons are in the valence shell of the boron atom?

options.text: 6 electrons, as boron forms three bonding pairs and has no lone pair
8 electrons, as one B–Cl bond must be a double bond to give boron an octet
3 electrons, as boron has three valence electrons of its own
2 electrons, as boron transfers three electrons to chlorine, leaving 1s²

questions.explanation: Each of boron's three valence electrons pairs with one from a chlorine atom, giving three B–Cl bonding pairs and no lone pair: 3 × 2 = 6 electrons, fewer than an octet. Each Cl has one bonding pair and three lone pairs, eight electrons.

questions.stem: The O–O bond in hydrogen peroxide, H₂O₂, has a length of 148 pm; the O=O bond in oxygen, O₂, has a length of 121 pm. Which statement about the strengths of these two bonds is correct?

options.text: O=O is weaker, as the two shared pairs between the nuclei repel each other strongly
O=O is weaker, as oxygen reacts so readily, for example in combustion reactions
O=O is stronger, as two shared pairs attract both nuclei more than one
The two bonds have the same strength, as both are between two oxygen atoms

questions.explanation: Two shared pairs between the nuclei mean more negative charge attracting both nuclei, so they are pulled closer (121 pm against 148 pm) and more energy is needed to separate them: O=O about 498 kJ mol⁻¹ against O–O about 144 kJ mol⁻¹. Shorter and stronger go together.

questions.stem: In the vapour at lower temperatures, aluminium chloride exists as Al₂Cl₆ molecules, formed when two AlCl₃ units join through two bridging chlorine atoms. Which describes the new bonds that join the two units?

options.text: A lone pair on the aluminium atom of each unit is donated to a chlorine atom of the other unit
A lone pair on a chlorine atom of each unit is donated to the aluminium atom of the other
Al³⁺ ions in one unit attract Cl⁻ ions in the other unit, forming two ionic bonds
Each new bond forms from one electron of an aluminium atom and one of a chlorine atom

questions.stem: Ionic radii (pm): Na⁺ 102, Cs⁺ 167, Ca²⁺ 100, Ba²⁺ 135, F⁻ 133, O²⁻ 140, S²⁻ 184. Which compound has the largest lattice enthalpy?

options.text: NaF
CsF
BaS
CaO

questions.explanation: Lattice enthalpy increases with ion charge and decreases with ion radius. CaO and BaS contain 2+ and 2− ions, which attract far more strongly than the 1+ and 1− ions of NaF and CsF. Of the two, CaO has the smaller ions (sum of radii 240 pm against 319 pm), so its lattice enthalpy is the largest.

questions.stem: In the Lewis formula of ethanal, CH₃CHO, the carbonyl carbon is bonded to the methyl carbon, one H atom and the O atom. How many lone pairs are on the oxygen atom?

options.text: 2 lone pairs, as 4 of the 18 valence electrons remain after the C–C, C–H and C=O bonds
4 lone pairs, as O gains two electrons from C and is an O²⁻ ion with an octet
3 lone pairs, as the C=O double bond is one shared pair, so O needs three more
0 lone pairs, as a Lewis formula shows only the bonding pairs between the atoms

questions.explanation: Ethanal has 2 × 4 + 4 × 1 + 6 = 18 valence electrons. One C–C bond, four C–H bonds and a C=O double bond use 14, leaving 4, which form two lone pairs on O. O then has 4 + 4 = 8 electrons, and each C has 8.

questions.stem: How does the carbon–carbon bond in ethyne, HC≡CH, compare with the carbon–carbon bond in ethane, CH₃CH₃?

options.text: It is longer and stronger
It is shorter and weaker
It is longer and weaker
It is shorter and stronger

questions.explanation: A triple bond has three shared pairs between the nuclei, against one in the single bond. More shared electrons attract both nuclei more strongly, pulling them closer (C≡C 120 pm, C–C 154 pm) and making the bond harder to break (839 against 346 kJ mol⁻¹).

questions.stem: Ammonia, NH₃, reacts with a hydrogen ion, H⁺, to form the ammonium ion, NH₄⁺. Which statement about the bonds in NH₄⁺ is correct?

options.text: The bond formed from the lone pair on nitrogen is longer and weaker than the other three N–H bonds
The new bond formed from a pair of electrons supplied by the H⁺ ion to nitrogen
The new bond formed from one electron supplied by nitrogen and one electron supplied by H⁺
All four N–H bonds are identical, although one formed from the lone pair on nitrogen

questions.stem: Lattice enthalpy is a measure of the strength of the ionic bonding in a compound. Ionic radii (pm): Na⁺ 102, K⁺ 138, F⁻ 133, Cl⁻ 181. Which shows the lattice enthalpies of NaF, NaCl and KCl in decreasing order?

options.text: KCl > NaCl > NaF
NaF > NaCl > KCl
NaF > KCl > NaCl
NaF = NaCl = KCl

questions.explanation: All three compounds contain 1+ and 1− ions, so the radii decide. The sums of the radii are NaF 235 pm, NaCl 283 pm and KCl 319 pm; the closer the ion centres, the stronger the attraction, so NaF > NaCl > KCl.

questions.stem: What holds the hydrogen atom and the chlorine atom together in a molecule of hydrogen chloride, HCl?

options.text: The need of each atom to gain a full outer shell by sharing a pair of electrons
The shared pair of electrons itself, acting as a physical link between the atoms
The electrostatic attraction of both nuclei to a shared pair of electrons
The electrostatic attraction between the oppositely charged ions H⁺ and Cl⁻

questions.explanation: The shared pair lies between the H and Cl nuclei and is attracted to both of them. This electrostatic attraction holds the two atoms together, and it is what a covalent bond is.

questions.stem: Sodium chloride has a very low volatility: it does not evaporate at room temperature and melts only at 801 °C. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Every ion is strongly attracted to many ions of opposite charge.
Its particles are so heavy that they cannot move fast enough to escape.
Evaporating it would break the strong bond in every NaCl molecule.
Sodium is a metal with a high boiling point, and NaCl keeps this property.

questions.explanation: In the lattice every ion is surrounded by ions of opposite charge and attracted to all of them. Separating the ions means overcoming many strong electrostatic attractions, which needs a large amount of energy, so sodium chloride has a low volatility.

questions.stem: The formula of magnesium chloride is MgCl₂. What does this formula represent?

options.text: One molecule of one Mg atom bonded to two Cl atoms
Mg²⁺ ions combined 1 : 1 with chlorine molecules, Cl₂
A Mg atom sharing an electron pair with each Cl atom
The 1 : 2 ratio of Mg²⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in a lattice

questions.explanation: Ionic compounds exist as three-dimensional lattices, and their formulas are empirical formulas: MgCl₂ gives the simplest whole-number ratio of the ions, one Mg²⁺ for every two Cl⁻.
